questions.statement: Students who want to specialize in a specific field often choose a ______ as their primary area of study.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A minor is a secondary area of study.
Correct. A major is the main subject studied by a college student.
Incorrect. An elective is an optional course.
Incorrect. A syllabus is an outline of a course.

questions.explanation:
'Major' is the standard academic term for a student's principal subject of study in higher education.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: By the time you graduate, you will have gained valuable experience through your internships.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Present simple.
Incorrect. Simple future.
Correct. Future perfect for an action completed by a specific future point.
Incorrect. Present perfect.

questions.explanation:
The future perfect 'will have gained' describes an achievement that will be a completed fact at the time of graduation.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: A well-written curriculum vitae (CV) should highlight your skills and relevant work history.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Obscure means to hide.
Correct. To highlight means to draw attention to or emphasize.
Incorrect. To dismiss means to ignore or reject.
Incorrect. To fabricate means to invent or lie.

questions.explanation:
'Highlight' is the appropriate verb for emphasizing positive attributes in a professional document.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: In a rapidly changing job market, the ability to adapt and learn new skills is essential for career longevity.

options.feedback: Correct. To adapt means to become adjusted to new conditions.
Incorrect. To stagnate means to stop developing.
Incorrect. To surrender means to give up.
Incorrect. Resisting change is usually negative in this context.

questions.explanation:
'Adapt' correctly identifies the proactive behavior needed to succeed in an evolving professional environment.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: The author argues that while university provides theoretical knowledge, vocational training offers practical skills.
questions.context: Debate on the value of a university degree versus vocational training.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Redundant means unnecessary.
Incorrect. Abstract means existing in thought but not having a physical existence.
Correct. Practical skills are those related to real-world application.
Incorrect. Obsolete means out of date.

questions.explanation:
'Practical' is the term that best contrasts with 'theoretical' in the context of professional training.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: A scholarship is a grant or payment made to support a student's education, awarded on the basis of academic achievement.

options.feedback: Incorrect. A loan must be paid back.
Correct. A scholarship is usually merit-based and does not need to be repaid.
Incorrect. A mortgage is a loan for a house.
Incorrect. A dividend is a sum of money paid to shareholders.

questions.explanation:
'Scholarship' is the specific term for merit-based financial support for students.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: If I were you, I would research the company thoroughly before the interview.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Present tense.
Correct. Subjunctive 'were' is used in second conditional advice.
Incorrect. 'Were' is preferred in formal conditional structures.
Incorrect. Third conditional.

questions.explanation:
The phrase 'If I were you' is a standard second conditional structure for giving advice.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: Networking allows professionals to exchange information and develop contacts which may lead to career advancement.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Isolation is the opposite of networking.
Correct. Networking is the process of interacting with others to exchange information.
Incorrect. While competition exists, the act of developing contacts is networking.
Incorrect. Withdrawal means pulling away.

questions.explanation:
'Networking' is the term used for building professional relationships that can benefit one's career.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: She regrets not studying harder during her senior year.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Regret is usually followed by a gerund for past actions.
Correct. 'Regret + (not) -ing' is used to talk about things we wish we hadn't (or had) done in the past.
Incorrect. Base form doesn't fit.
Incorrect. Incorrect grammar.

questions.explanation:
The gerund 'studying' after 'regrets' describes the action being regretted.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: While "hard skills" are specific technical abilities, "soft skills" like communication and empathy are increasingly valued by employers.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says they are valued.
Incorrect. While some are innate, they can also be developed.
Correct. Increasingly means more and more.
Incorrect. Barely means hardly at all.

questions.explanation:
'Increasingly' captures the trend of employers placing higher value on interpersonal skills.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: The CEO is the highest-ranking person in a company and is responsible for making major corporate decisions.

options.feedback: Incorrect. An intern is a low-level student worker.
Incorrect. A supervisor manages a specific team.
Correct. Chief Executive Officer.
Incorrect. A client is someone who buys services.

questions.explanation:
'CEO' is the acronym for the top executive position in most organizations.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: I may consider taking a gap year after high school to travel and gain perspective.

options.feedback: Correct. 'Consider' is followed by a gerund.
Incorrect. Infinitive is not used after 'consider'.
Incorrect. Base form doesn't fit.
Incorrect. Past participle.

questions.explanation:
The verb 'consider' requires the gerund form of the following verb.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: Candidates who meet all the requirements will be invited for an interview.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Ignoring requirements won't get an interview.
Correct. To meet a requirement means to fulfill it.
Incorrect. Neglect means to fail to care for.
Incorrect. Postpone means to delay.

questions.explanation:
'Meet' is the standard verb used for fulfilling criteria or requirements.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: You won't get a promotion unless you show more initiative in your work.

options.feedback: Incorrect. 'If you show' would mean the promotion is certain if initiative is shown, but 'unless' expresses the condition better here.
Correct. 'Unless' means 'if not' and is used to express a negative condition.
Incorrect. Expresses contrast.
Incorrect. Expresses choice between alternatives.

questions.explanation:
'Unless' is used to indicate that the promotion depends on the condition of showing initiative.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: The article concludes that workers must continuously upskill to remain competitive in an automated world.
questions.context: Conclusion of an article on job automation.

options.feedback: Correct. To upskill means to learn new skills or teach workers new skills.
Incorrect. Retiring doesn't help one remain competitive.
Incorrect. Complaining is not a strategy for competitiveness.
Incorrect. Downsizing usually refers to companies cutting staff.

questions.explanation:
'Upskill' is the precise term for acquiring new and relevant professional skills to stay current in the market.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: A freelancer is a person who is self-employed and is not committed to a particular employer long-term.

options.feedback: Incorrect. An apprentice is learning a trade.
Correct. A freelancer works for themselves on a project-by-project basis.
Incorrect. A volunteer works for free.
Incorrect. A subordinate is someone under someone else's authority.

questions.explanation:
'Freelancer' is the standard term for independent professionals who sell their services to multiple clients.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: He suggested that she apply for the management position.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Present simple doesn't fit the 'that' clause here.
Correct. Subjunctive form after 'suggested'.
Incorrect. Infinitive doesn't fit the 'that' clause.
Incorrect. Gerund doesn't fit the 'that' clause.

questions.explanation:
Verbs like 'suggest' and 'recommend' are followed by a 'that' clause with the base form of the verb (subjunctive mood).

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: Effective collaboration within a team can significantly improve the quality of a project.
questions.context: Benefits of working in a team.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Isolation prevents teamwork.
Correct. Collaboration means working together to achieve a goal.
Incorrect. Negligence means lack of care.
Incorrect. Friction means conflict or disagreement.

questions.explanation:
'Collaboration' is the positive process of multiple people working together effectively.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: I hope to have finished my master's degree by the time I turn thirty.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Simple infinitive.
Incorrect. Gerund.
Correct. Perfect infinitive indicates an action completed before a certain time.
Incorrect. While common, 'to have finished' better fits the 'by the time' structure.

questions.explanation:
The perfect infinitive 'to have finished' expresses a completed action relative to a future point.

---
questions.subject: Ingles

questions.statement: Ultimately, a career should provide not only financial stability but also personal fulfillment.
questions.context: Conclusion of an essay on work-life balance.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Frustration is negative.
Incorrect. Exhaustion is negative.
Correct. Fulfillment means the achievement of something desired or promised.
Incorrect. Stagnancy is negative.

questions.explanation: 'Fulfillment' refers to the satisfaction and sense of accomplishment derived from one's work.
